title: How often jump-up bands played funerals and who hired them
summary: Miller says about four funerals a month, bands going out of town on weekends, Monday-night dances, and clubs and societies hiring leaders for funerals.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: How many times did y'all work and say, a guy like Rene, a buddy, or you, would you work how many times a week in the street?
In the street? Oh, would that call it a funeral? Well, like in, like Labor Day, Mardi Gras, 4th of July, or somebody died, you know, we'll play a funeral.
But how many funerals would you play? In a week? Well, I'd say in a week, a month, a year, or whatever.
Well, maybe a month. I'd say you'd play about four.
About four funerals. Well, that's about once a week, in other words. You'd be out in the street. So there was a lot of work for jump-up bands.

Oh, yeah. Well, you see, we did write some out here in New Orleans, but the average time, these bands was going away from town. One, Bugaloosers, Gary, out in the country, La Plague, anywhere. All of them was going on weekends like that. And Monday nights, well, economy, co-op, Riddling, Aging Park, Napoleon Avenue Hall, everybody would be playing Monday night in a different hall, see. And them that wasn't going out of town, they'd be on the streets all day Sunday, you know, advertising for dances in town, you see. You'd have seven or eight, ten or twelve dances going on in town, but four bands leave towns and going somewhere to play, see. There's a lot of bands, yeah.
Well, what kind of organization would hire a jump-up band for a funeral rather than an organized band?
Well, them societies and clubs. They'd just go hire him if he's a leader of a band. Say, we want you to clear a funeral. Okay, well, you get the men together.
But didn't some of them have contracts with some of the organized bands? Nothing.
They wouldn't hire the same band year after year. They'd switch around.
Well, maybe for a carnival, they would. I'd wait for the buzzards for about three or four years. Every year for carnival.
